title: Health Insurance for Your Residence Permit: What Is Accepted in Türkiye
excerpt: Which health insurance the migration authority accepts for a residence permit — Turkish private policies, social security agreements, SGK — the wording a private policy must carry, and who is exempt.
bodyHtml:
Most residence permit applications need valid health insurance. The wrong kind can hold an application up, so it's worth knowing exactly what the Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi) accepts.

This guide summarises the migration authority's published document requirements. It is practical information, not legal or insurance advice — requirements can change, and your personalised e-İkamet checklist is the final word for your application.

The basic rule

Your health insurance must cover the whole residence permit period you are applying for. A policy that runs out earlier than the permit you're asking for won't do.

For a long-term residence permit, you need health insurance of at least one year.

What counts

A private health insurance policy

  • A policy from an insurer in Türkiye is the usual route. Brokers (acente) sell policies written for residence-permit applications.

  • A private policy taken out abroad is only valid if it was issued through the insurer's branch or agency in Türkiye. A travel insurance policy from home generally won't meet the requirement.

  • The policy must state, in Turkish, that it covers the minimum coverage set by Circular No. 9 of 6 June 2014 on private health insurance for residence permit applications: "İşbu poliçe 06/06/2014 tarih ve 9 sayılı ikamet izni taleplerinde yaptırılacak özel sağlık sigortalarına ilişkin genelgede belirlenen asgari teminat yapısını kapsamaktadır." Check that this sentence is on your policy before you pay.

  • At a first application, bring the original policy — e-signed, or signed and stamped. For an extension, a certified copy goes in your file.

Social security agreements

If you're covered under a bilateral social security agreement between your country and Türkiye, have your status confirmed by the provincial social security (SGK) office and add that signed and stamped document to your application.

SGK (general health insurance)

If you're covered by Türkiye's general health insurance through SGK, the provision document you bring must be stamped and signed — and for a family permit, it must cover the family members too. For how and when foreign residents can join SGK, see our healthcare guide.

Family permits

For a family residence permit, the supporting family member's health insurance must cover every family member on the application.

Who doesn't need it

  • Under 18 or over 65: the health insurance requirement doesn't apply — but if you already have a valid policy, you must submit it.

  • Students: students can ask to join general health insurance (GSS) within three months of registering at their university. If they do, health insurance isn't requested for the application — but they must join GSS within those three months and notify the migration office.

  • Public coverage: if your health costs during your stay are covered by the relevant public institutions, the requirement doesn't apply.

Before you buy

  • Match the policy's dates to the permit period you're requesting.

  • Check for the Circular No. 9 sentence.

  • Make sure the name and passport number match your application exactly.

  • Keep the original and digital copies — you'll need the policy again at renewal.

If you're unsure which applies to you, ask the Foreigners Communication Centre, YİMER 157, or your provincial migration directorate before you buy.
